name: ICE catheter robot
full_name: Harvard 4-DOF robotic ultrasound (ICE) catheter steering system
group: Harvard SEAS (R. D. Howe; P. M. Loschak, A. Degirmenci) with MIT Lincoln Laboratory (L. J. Brattain) and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (C. M. Tschabrunn, E. Anter)
versions: 2017 TRO algorithms for automatically pointing ICE catheters, benchtop (full, PMC author manuscript); 2020 IJRR in-vivo automatic steering with respiratory motion compensation (full, loschak2020_automatically); earlier in vivo navigation study Degirmenci et al. 2016 (cited in loschak2020 Sec. 1, not read)
target_anatomy: intracardiac echocardiography in the heart chambers
devices_driven: AcuNav 10 Fr (3.30 mm) 110 cm ICE catheter with 64-element array (Biosense Webster) (TRO 2017 Sec. II)
n_dof_detail: 4 (pitch knob, yaw knob, handle roll, handle translation)
translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (lead-screw translation stage carries the whole handle)
rotation_detail: motor grounded to the stage turns the handle by timing belt; two handle-mounted motors turn the knobs by timing belts
imaging_compat: ICE ultrasound; EM tracking of instrument tip in tests; IJRR 2020: four EM trackers (two on the US catheter, one on the target catheter, one on the chest wall for respiration) (Sec. 3.2)
validation_detail: 2017: benchtop water tank with gelatin left-atrium phantom; 2020: one 64 kg live pig, US catheter via a 14 Fr femoral-vein introducer into the right atrium, target 6 Fr quadpolar catheter in the left ventricle, heart paced at 120 bpm; volume-imaging steps (18 steps, 133 s), instrument tracking (329 s) and tracking a manually steered target (431 s) (IJRR 2020 Sec. 3.2-3.3)
key_numbers: benchtop position RMS 1.9 mm; imager spinning 0.25 deg RMS with 1.0 mm tip drift; 3-D pointing 1.6 mm and 0.17 deg RMS; test speeds <= 1 mm/s and <= 0.5 deg/s; 6.5 W brushed DC motors with Maxon EPOS2 (TRO 2017); in vivo 1.05 mm and 1.33 deg mean absolute error with respiratory compensation (IJRR 2020 abstract); in vivo step imaging 2.56 mm / 0.98 deg MAE over 134 s of well-modelled breathing, 6.59 mm / 2.27 deg when the model was outdated; manual-target tracking 2.81 deg MAE and 2.14 mm position MAE over 431 s (Sec. 3.3)
